title: 6 best Tipalti alternatives in the UAE in 2026
summary: The best Tipalti alternative for UAE businesses in 2026 is Alaan, which handles vendor payments, corporate cards, receipt capture, and accounting sync in one platform built for UAE VAT rules, with a free starter plan.
body_markdown:
Tipalti is very good at one thing: paying a lot of suppliers in a lot of countries. The trouble for many UAE finance teams is that this isn't the thing eating their week. It's the AED 300 taxi receipts, the Meta ad spend on someone's personal card, and the supplier invoice that arrived without a TRN.


That's usually when teams start looking at Tipalti alternatives, and specifically at[spend management platforms built for UAE finance teams](https://www.alaan.com/products/expense-management) that cover supplier payments and employee spend in one place.


In this guide, we'll cover what Tipalti does well, where it falls short for UAE businesses, and the six best Tipalti alternatives in 2026, with features, pricing, and trade-offs for each.


The best Tipalti alternative for most UAE businesses is Alaan, followed by BILL for teams that mainly need AP and AR automation and Payoneer for low-cost cross-border payouts. Here's the full shortlist:


Tool Best for


Alaan Vendor payments, corporate cards, expenses, and accounting sync in one UAE platform


BILL AP, AR, and spend management under one login


Payoneer Pay-as-you-go payouts to suppliers and contractors abroad


Spendesk Approvals, reimbursements, and supplier invoices in one workflow


Rydoo Receipt-to-reimbursement automation for multi-country teams


HSBC Virtual Card Large-value supplier payments for existing HSBC clients


## 1. Alaan


**Best for:** UAE businesses that want supplier payments and employee spend handled in the same place, with UAE VAT data captured on every transaction.


**Similar to:** BILL, Spendesk.


Alaan is a UAE spend management platform that combines Visa corporate cards, vendor payments, expense management, and accounting automation. More than 3,000 businesses across the Middle East use it, and it holds a 4.7 rating on[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/alaan/reviews) , with reviewers scoring it 97% for ease of use.


Where Tipalti starts with the supplier invoice, Alaan starts with the question of how money leaves the business, whether that's a bank transfer to a supplier in Mumbai or a card swipe at a Dubai print shop.


### Vendor and contractor payments


You can[pay international vendors and contractors](https://www.alaan.com/blog/overseas-business-payments) through Visa Direct, with approval workflows and automated invoice extraction built in.[SuperPay](https://www.alaan.com/superpay) handles global invoice payments with a focus on keeping FX costs low and 0 transfer fees.


With the[Business Account add-on](https://www.alaan.com/business-banking) , you get a dedicated IBAN to receive funds and send domestic bank transfers, plus AP automation that reads incoming bills so nobody has to retype them.


### Corporate cards for everything that isn't an invoice


A lot of supplier spend never comes as an invoice: SaaS subscriptions, ad platforms, and the odd urgent purchase. Alaan lets you[issue physical and virtual Visa cards](https://www.alaan.com/supercard) , lock them to merchant categories, and set daily or monthly limits before anyone spends.


Premium adds unlimited 2% cashback on international spend and up to 1% on domestic spend.[invygo](https://www.alaan.com/customer-stories/invygo) , a Dubai car subscription company, has earned more than AED 150,000 in cashback after moving its ad and software spend onto Alaan cards.


### Receipts and VAT data captured at the source


Employees submit receipts through the app, WhatsApp, or email, and Alaan chases anything missing. Its[AI pulls out the supplier's TRN](https://www.alaan.com/products/alaan-intelligence) , the VAT amount, and merchant details, then flags duplicates and out-of-policy spend.


That's the data the FTA's new supplier checks lean on, and it's much easier to collect at the moment of spend than to reconstruct before a VAT return.


### Accounting sync with UAE tools and global ERPs


Alaan connects directly to Xero, QuickBooks, Zoho Books, Wafeq, Odoo, and ERPNext, with Dynamics 365, NetSuite, and SAP on Premium. Expenses and bills arrive coded based on rules you set once. Here's more on how[Alaan's accounting automation](https://www.alaan.com/products/accounting-automation) works at month-end.


### Alaan's pricing


Alaan has three plans:


- **Starter:** AED 0/month for up to 10 users, with multiple cards, receipt verification, approval workflows, cross-border transfers, and core accounting integrations.
- **Premium:** AED 499/month (currently with 3 months free), adding unlimited users, cashback, ERP integrations, AI features, and a Customer Success Manager.
- **Enterprise:** Custom pricing, adding dedicated implementation, custom ERP and API integrations, and multi-entity support.


The Business Account and AP automation add-on costs an extra AED 79/month.


### Pros and cons


✅ Supplier payments, cards, and expenses in one platform instead of three.


✅ 0 transfer fees on international payments


✅ Built around UAE requirements like TRN capture and local accounting tools such as Wafeq.


✅ Public pricing in AED with a free starter plan.


✅ Unlimited 2% international cashback on Premium.


❌ It isn't built for mass payouts to thousands of payees, like marketplace sellers or affiliates, where Tipalti is stronger.


❌ The Alaan card is currently only available to employees of UAE businesses, which matters for groups with staff abroad.


## 2. BILL


**Best for:** Businesses whose main job is accounts payable and receivable, with spend management as a secondary need.


**Similar to:** Tipalti.


BILL is the closest like-for-like Tipalti alternative on this list. It covers AP, AR, and spend management under one login, with card spend running through its Divvy card.


### Features


- **AP automation:** Bill capture, approval routing, and payments from one dashboard.
- **AR and invoicing:** Send invoices and track what customers owe alongside what you owe suppliers.
- **Spend management:** Budgets, card controls, and real-time spend tracking.
- **Accounting sync:** Two-way sync with major accounting software from the Team plan up.


### Pricing


BILL's financial operations plans start at $49/user/month for Essentials, then $65 for Team and $89 for Corporate, with custom Enterprise pricing.


### Pros and cons


✅ Covers both sides of the ledger, payables and receivables.


✅ Lower entry price than Tipalti for small AP teams.


❌ Built for the US market, so confirm what's available to a UAE-registered entity first.


❌ Per-user pricing grows quickly once you add approvers.


## 3. Payoneer


**Best for:** Businesses that mainly need to pay overseas suppliers and contractors without a monthly subscription.


**Similar to:** Tipalti (Mass Payments).


Payoneer is a[cross-border payments platform](https://www.alaan.com/blog/global-b2b-cross-border-payments-platform) used by a lot of UAE freelancers, agencies, and e-commerce sellers. It lets you[send business payments in local currency to suppliers and contractors in 190+ countries](https://www.payoneer.com/send-payments/) , one at a time or as a bulk file.


### Features


- **Bulk payouts:** Upload one file to pay multiple suppliers across several countries and currencies.
- **Receiving accounts:** Local receiving details in major currencies, useful if you also get paid by overseas clients.
- **Fee shown upfront:** The exchange rate and fee appear before you confirm each payment.


### Pricing


[Payoneer uses transaction-based pricing](https://www.payoneer.com/pricing/) with no monthly subscription. Fees depend on the payment method, currency, and corridor, and an annual account fee can apply to low-activity accounts.


### Pros and cons


✅ No platform fee, so it's cheap to start for low payment volumes.


✅ Simple setup compared with a full AP platform.


❌ No real AP workflow: invoice capture, PO matching, and multi-step approvals sit elsewhere.


❌ FX and transfer fees can add up at higher volumes.


## 4. Spendesk


**Best for:** Teams that want spend requests, reimbursements, and supplier invoices in one approval workflow.


**Similar to:** Alaan, Rydoo.


Spendesk is a spend management platform that combines employee spending, reimbursements, and invoice processing. Its OCR reads receipt and invoice details automatically.


### Features


- **Invoice management:** Capture, approve, and pay supplier invoices alongside employee spend.
- **Duplicate invoice detection:** Catches repeated invoices and common errors before payment.
- **Real-time monitoring:** Finance sees missing receipts and errors as they happen.


### Pricing


[Spendesk uses custom pricing](https://www.spendesk.com/pricing/) , so you'll need a sales call for a quote.


### Pros and cons


✅ Invoices and employee spend in one tool.


✅ Solid budgeting controls by team or department.


❌ No public pricing.


❌ Built primarily for European businesses, so check card availability and VAT handling for a UAE entity.


## 5. Rydoo


**Best for:** Multi-country companies where employee reimbursements are the bigger problem than supplier payments.


**Similar to:** Spendesk.


Rydoo is an expense management tool built around receipt scanning and reimbursements, with tax, per diem, and mileage rules for more than 80 countries. It also offers[AI-driven AP automation via Semine](https://www.rydoo.com/accounts-payable/) as an add-on.


### Features


- **Receipt scanning:** Turns a photo into a submitted expense in seconds.
- **Smart Audit:** AI flags errors and policy breaches, included on the Enterprise plan.
- **Card reconciliation:** Matches transactions from Visa, Mastercard, and Amex cards on Pro and above.


### Pricing


According to[Rydoo's pricing page](https://www.rydoo.com/pricing/) , Essentials is $9/user/month and Pro is $11/user/month, billed annually. Business and Enterprise are custom-priced.


### Pros and cons


✅ Employees find it quick to use, which helps adoption.


✅ Strong multi-country expense compliance.


❌ AP is an add-on rather than the core product, so it isn't a direct Tipalti replacement on its own.


❌ Rydoo's own cards are only included from the Business plan.


## 6. HSBC Virtual Card


**Best for:** Large companies already banking with HSBC that want card-based supplier payments.


**Similar to:** Other bank-issued commercial card programs.


HSBC lets businesses generate single-use and multi-use virtual card numbers to pay suppliers through its online portal.


### Features


- **Unique card numbers:** A new number per supplier or transaction limits fraud exposure.
- **Reconciliation reporting:** Custom data fields for tracking supplier spend.
- **Fraud protection:** Zero-liability protection on each virtual card.


### Pricing


HSBC doesn't publish pricing, so you'll need to go through the bank's application process.


### Pros and cons


✅ Bank-grade security for large-value supplier payments.


✅ Easy fit if your treasury is already with HSBC.


❌ Only works for suppliers that accept card payments.


❌ No invoice capture or approval workflows, so you'll still need an AP tool.


## How to choose the right Tipalti alternative


Pull last month's outgoing payments and sort them into three piles by count, not value: supplier invoices paid by transfer, card transactions, and employee reimbursements. The biggest pile tells you which kind of tool you need.


We do this exercise with a lot of UAE finance teams, and the result usually surprises them. A company might send 40 supplier transfers a month but run 600 card transactions, and it's the 600 that generate the receipt-chasing, VAT coding, and month-end stress.


- **Supplier invoices are the biggest pile:** Stay with an AP-first tool like Tipalti or BILL, or use Alaan if you also want cards in the same system.
- **Card transactions are the biggest pile:** A card-first platform like Alaan will save more hours than any AP tool.
- **Reimbursements are the biggest pile:** Rydoo or Spendesk, or move that spend onto company cards so the pile shrinks.
- **You pay thousands of payees in dozens of countries:** Tipalti is probably still the right tool, and this list may not be for you.


A few more checks before you sign anything:


1. **Does it capture the supplier's TRN and VAT amount automatically?** You'll need that data for input VAT recovery and the FTA's supplier checks.
2. **Does it integrate directly with your accounting software?** Wafeq, Zoho Books, and Odoo are common in the UAE and not every global tool supports them.
3. **What does a payment actually cost?** Add the platform fee, per-payment fees, and FX markup for a typical month, not just the headline price.
4. **Who approves what?** Make sure approval rules can follow how your business actually works, by amount, department, or supplier.


## Summing it up


Tipalti is built for companies whose biggest finance job is paying large numbers of suppliers around the world. Most UAE businesses look elsewhere because their week is shaped by card spend, receipts, and VAT data as much as by supplier invoices.


If you want supplier payments, cards, and expenses in one platform priced in AED, Alaan is the strongest Tipalti alternative for UAE businesses in 2026. BILL is the closer swap if AP and AR are all you need, and Payoneer works for occasional overseas payouts without a subscription.


The three-pile exercise above takes about 20 minutes and will tell you more than any demo. If card spend turns out to be your biggest pile,[book a demo with Alaan](https://www.alaan.com/demo) and we'll show you how it would run on our platform.


Before you book six demos, it helps to know what the software is supposed to do once it's live, and our guide on[how AP automation actually works](https://www.alaan.com/blog/ap-automation-accounts-payable-system) covers the whole flow from invoice capture to payment, plus the problems it won't fix for you.


## FAQs


**What is the best alternative to Tipalti in the UAE?**


For most UAE businesses, Alaan is the best Tipalti alternative because it handles vendor payments, corporate cards, expenses, and accounting sync in one platform, with UAE VAT data captured on each transaction and a free Starter plan.


**Is there a cheaper alternative to Tipalti?**


Yes. Alaan's Starter plan is free for up to 10 users, and Payoneer has no monthly fee, charging per transaction instead. Tipalti's accounts payable plans start at $99/month before transaction fees.


**Does Tipalti work for UAE VAT?**


Tipalti can process invoices from UAE suppliers, but much of its built-in tax tooling targets US forms like W-9s. UAE teams should check how any tool captures TRNs and VAT amounts for input VAT recovery.


**Which Tipalti alternative is best for paying international suppliers?**


Alaan supports international vendor payments through Visa Direct and SuperPay alongside cards and expenses. If you only need payouts and no AP workflow, Payoneer is a lighter option.


**Can I replace Tipalti with an expense management tool?**


Only if most of your outgoing payments are employee spend rather than supplier invoices. If you still pay a meaningful number of invoices, choose a platform that covers both, or keep a dedicated AP tool.
